name: Edale to Kinder Scout
summary: Classic Dark Peak circuit: up Grindsbrook Clough, west along the gritstone edges to Kinder Low and the 636 m summit, then down Jacob’s Ladder and back to Edale on the Pennine Way.
gradeNote: Steep, rocky scramble in upper Grindsbrook Clough; exposed moorland plateau where navigation is hard in mist; peat bog around the summit.
map: OS Explorer OL1 – The Peak District: Dark Peak area
start: Edale railway station (Hope Valley line); village car park next to the station
attribution: Route compiled from published OS grid references of landmarks; intermediate points and most heights are approximate. Always carry OS Explorer OL1 and a compass.

waypoints.name: Edale station
waypoints.description: Start at Edale station on the Hope Valley line (Manchester–Sheffield). The village car park is beside it.
waypoints.directions: Walk north up the lane through the village, under the railway and past the church, to the Old Nag’s Head.
waypoints.source: Pennine Way start grid ref next to the station, peakdistrictwalks.net

waypoints.name: The Old Nag’s Head
waypoints.description: Historic inn at Grindsbrook Booth and the official southern start of the Pennine Way.
waypoints.directions: Just past the inn, follow the path signed for Grindsbrook down to the footbridge over Grinds Brook.

waypoints.name: Grinds Brook footbridge
waypoints.description: Footbridge over Grinds Brook at the bottom of the valley.
waypoints.directions: Climb the stone steps and follow the path north-west through meadows and woodland into Grindsbrook Clough, crossing the brook where needed. The upper clough is a steep, rocky scramble up the stream bed — slippery when wet and best avoided when the brook is in spate.

waypoints.name: Top of Grindsbrook Clough
waypoints.description: You reach the edge of the Kinder plateau at about 590 m.
waypoints.directions: Turn left (west) on the path along the southern edge of the plateau towards the head of Crowden Clough.

waypoints.name: Crowden Brook crossing
waypoints.description: Ford Crowden Brook where it drops off the plateau into Crowden Clough.
waypoints.directions: Cross the brook and climb the short distance to the gritstone tor of Crowden Tower.

waypoints.name: Crowden Tower
waypoints.description: A fortress-like pile of gritstone guarding the head of Crowden Clough, with views down the Vale of Edale.
waypoints.directions: Continue west along the edge path into the field of weathered boulders known as the Woolpacks.

waypoints.name: The Woolpacks
waypoints.description: Wind-sculpted gritstone boulders, some with names such as the Pagoda and the Moat Stone.
waypoints.directions: Weave through the boulders and keep to the edge path, emerging at Pym Chair.

waypoints.name: Pym Chair
waypoints.description: Prominent gritstone outcrop on the edge path, at the western end of the Woolpacks.
waypoints.directions: Stay on the edge path heading west towards the anvil-shaped Noe Stool.
waypoints.source: Moors for the Future audio trail, SK 08797 87065

waypoints.name: Noe Stool
waypoints.description: Anvil-shaped rock above Edale Head, where the River Noe begins.
waypoints.directions: Bear north-west up the edge to the trig pillar on Kinder Low.

waypoints.name: Kinder Low trig point
waypoints.description: Trig pillar on a boulder at 633 m — once thought to be the top of Kinder.
waypoints.directions: For the true summit, head north-east (grid bearing about 050°) for about 750 m across peat groughs on faint paths. Only go in good visibility, and come back the same way.
waypoints.source: Trig pillar SK 07899 87062, britishwalks.org; height 633 m

waypoints.name: Kinder Scout summit
waypoints.description: The highest point in the Peak District (636 m on OS maps; a 2009 survey suggests nearer 634 m). An unmarked, peaty knoll — easy to miss in mist.
waypoints.directions: Retrace your steps south-west to the Kinder Low trig pillar.

waypoints.name: Kinder Low (return)
waypoints.directions: Follow the Pennine Way south past the rocks of Swine’s Back to the cairn at the top of Jacob’s Ladder.

waypoints.name: Top of Jacob’s Ladder
waypoints.description: Cairn at the top of the old packhorse route. Edale Cross, a medieval wayside cross, is 350 m to the south-west.
waypoints.directions: Descend Jacob’s Ladder — the steep stepped path or the gentler zig-zag bridleway — to the packhorse bridge.

waypoints.name: Jacob’s Ladder packhorse bridge
waypoints.description: Stone packhorse bridge over the infant River Noe.
waypoints.directions: Follow the track east down the valley past Lee Farm.

waypoints.name: Lee Farm
waypoints.description: Hill farm in the upper Vale of Edale.
waypoints.directions: Continue along the lane to the hamlet of Upper Booth.

waypoints.name: Upper Booth
waypoints.description: Farming hamlet where Crowden Brook joins the River Noe.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Pennine Way signs north-east across the fields below Broadlee-Bank Tor back to Grindsbrook Booth.

waypoints.name: The Old Nag’s Head (return)
waypoints.directions: Walk back down the lane to the station.

pois.name: Edale Cross
pois.description: Medieval wayside cross on the old packhorse route, 350 m south-west of the top of Jacob’s Ladder.

pois.name: Grindslow Knoll
pois.description: Rounded top above Grindsbrook Clough — a short detour from the plateau edge with fine views over Edale.

sections.note: Summit detour: faint paths across peat groughs. Skip it in poor visibility — Kinder Low (633 m) makes a fine top.
